sweeps.angle: Angle 1: official Gemma 4 E2B facts (release, parameters/PLE, context, modalities, licence, QAT/GGUF checkpoints, sampling, thinking-mode template, thinking-off quality)

findings.claim: Gemma 4 E2B-it model card on Hugging Face states 2.3B effective parameters (5.1B with embeddings); Safetensors widget lists about 5B params.
findings.evidence: HF model card google/gemma-4-E2B-it: '2.3B effective (5.1B with embeddings)'. Per-Layer Embeddings give each decoder layer its own small embedding for every token; these tables are large but used only for lookups, so compute size is much smaller than the total.
findings.source_date: Card 'last updated 2026-07-30' per ai.google.dev mirror; HF page itself shows no release date
findings.implication_for_boar: RAM budget must be planned on the ~5.1B total weight footprint, not 2.3B; the 3.11 GB Q4_K_M file and 4.5-4.6 GB PSS peak on the Pixel 8a are consistent with that, so the 8 GB default case is plausible but the PLE tables are not free in memory.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 E2B has 35 layers, a 512-token sliding window, and 128K context.
findings.evidence: ai.google.dev Gemma 4 model card page: 'Architecture: 35 layers and a 512-token sliding window', 'Context length: 128K tokens'.
findings.source_date: page last updated 2026-07-30 per fetched text
findings.implication_for_boar: 128K context is far above what the app uses; the on-device context setting, not the model, is the constraint for KV memory on 8 GB.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 E2B accepts text, image and audio input (text output); vision encoder about 150M params, audio encoder about 300M; audio clips limited to 30 s; video handled as frame sequences.
findings.evidence: HF card: 'Text, Image, and Audio as input, with text output. The vision encoder is about 150M parameters and the audio encoder about 300M.' ai.google.dev card: 'Audio clips are limited to 30 seconds.'
findings.implication_for_boar: Text-only use is the BOAR case; the extra encoders add to file size and are not used by our English text Q&A path, unless we turn on image/audio later (out of scope for bounty #31).

findings.claim: Licence for Gemma 4 E2B is Apache 2.0 (not the earlier Gemma Terms of Use).
findings.evidence: HF card metadata 'apache-2.0'; ai.google.dev card: 'License: Apache 2.0'. Secondary press (Bernama, datanorth.ai, rits.shanghai.nyu.edu) also describe a shift from earlier Gemma terms to Apache 2.0.
findings.implication_for_boar: Licence is not a blocker for shipping a catalog entry or redistributing a GGUF; the maintainer's review of licence terms becomes a simple check (Apache-2.0 text plus NOTICE if any).

findings.claim: Gemma 4 release date reported as 2 April 2026 by press and Wikipedia; the official dates on the primary pages conflict.
findings.evidence: Bernama and Wikipedia-listed date: April 2, 2026 with a Google blog post (blog URL not found). Conflicting primary dates: Gemma 4 Technical Report arXiv:2607.02770 v1 submitted 2 Jul 2026, v2 revised 24 Jul 2026; ai.google.dev card 'Last updated 2026-07-30'; ggml-org collection 'Updated Jul 30'. Bedrock page gives 'Jun 10, 2025' for E2B, which is likely wrong.
findings.implication_for_boar: Do not quote a launch date in the maintainer package until the Google blog URL is found; the 2 Apr vs 2 Jul discrepancy may be a model-card refresh rather than a new release, so state it as unverified.

findings.claim: Thinking mode is enabled by putting the <|think|> token at the start of the system prompt; removing it disables thinking. When on, reasoning is emitted as a thought block before the answer.
findings.evidence: HF card: 'Thinking is enabled by including the <|think|> token at the start of the system prompt. To disable it, remove the token.' Reasoning appears as '<|channel>thought\n' followed by '<channel|>'. Transformers path: enable_thinking flag in apply_chat_template (sample uses enable_thinking=False).
findings.implication_for_boar: Our app's enable_thinking:false only works if the llama.cpp chat template maps that kwarg to the same switch; verify on the mini that the <|think|> token is absent from the prompt when thinking is off, otherwise the 'thinks by default' fix is unverified at the template level.

findings.claim: For E2B and E4B, disabled thinking does NOT produce an empty thought block; other Gemma 4 sizes do.
findings.evidence: ai.google.dev card: 'The empty-thought-block behavior for disabled thinking does not apply to E2B or E4B.' HF card: 'except for E2B and E4B, disabled thinking still produces an empty thought block.' The two summaries agree on the exception, which is the ambiguous part: E2B/E4B emit no empty block at all when thinking is off.
findings.implication_for_boar: Output parsing must handle a no-thought-block response for E2B; a parser that expects '<channel|>' to always be present would break on E2B.

findings.claim: Recommended sampling for Gemma 4 E2B-it: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64 for all use cases.
findings.evidence: HF card: 'temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, and top_k=64 for all use cases.' Unsloth QAT GGUF example uses --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64.
findings.implication_for_boar: Compare the engine's sampling (0.7/40/0.95/0.05) with the model-recommended 1.0/0.95/64 before attributing quality differences to the model; this is a cheap, testable knob.

findings.claim: Official Google QAT checkpoint exists as google/gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized, referenced by ggml-org conversions; no official QAT GGUF from ggml-org was found.
findings.evidence: ggml-org/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF lists source model 'google/gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized'. Files in that repo: Q4_0 2.84 GB, Q8_0 4.97 GB, BF16 9.31 GB (plus MTP files); no QAT-labelled GGUF.
findings.implication_for_boar: The official-tree GGUF is ggml-org Q4_0 (2.84 GB); a QAT Q4 path exists upstream via the Google checkpoint, but the GGUF for it comes from Unsloth, not Google/ggml-org. Our 3.11 GB unsloth Q4_K_M and the QAT file differ in provenance, which matters for a catalog entry.

findings.claim: Unsloth QAT GGUF for E2B: UD-Q4_K_XL at 2.62 GB, and a mobile-mixture UD-Q2_K_XL at 2.19 GB; naive Q4_0 conversion of the QAT checkpoint degraded accuracy (89.29% top-1, mean KLD 0.0511) while the Unsloth QAT GGUF reached 98.16% top-1 (KLD 0.0017).
findings.evidence: unsloth.ai/docs/models/gemma-4/qat: sizes and top-1/KLD numbers as quoted; the page itself gives no date.
findings.implication_for_boar: A quantization-quality claim from a third party (Unsloth, who ships the GGUF); a Q4_K_M from a plain conversion may lose more than the QAT path. Needs an independent measure on our dev set before the maintainer entry picks a quant.

findings.claim: A third-party QAT GGUF (leok7v) uses Q2_0 blocks and will not load in upstream llama.cpp.
findings.evidence: leok7v/gemma-4-e2b-it-qat HF card: 170 tensors use Q2_0, which is not upstream ggml (PrismML/Gadeon lineage).
findings.implication_for_boar: Do not pick that file for the catalog; the maintainer's build must load upstream b11010-era GGUF formats only.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 family is 2.3B-31B; E2B and E4B are the edge sizes; E4B is 4.5B effective; the 26B is MoE with 3.8B active and the 31B is dense 30.7B.
findings.evidence: Press summary of the Google announcement (datanorth.ai, Bernama) gives the lineup; E2B 2.3B effective and E4B 4.5B effective as on the primary card.
findings.implication_for_boar: E4B (4.5B effective, roughly 8B+ with PLE) is the next step up; it was the one the team measured as too slow on 8 GB class devices in the reference context, so E2B is the only edge size plausible at the 8 GB default.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 technical report (arXiv:2607.02770) states the suite includes a thinking mode that generates reasoning traces before responding; it does not report PLE details or thinking-off benchmark numbers in the abstract.
findings.evidence: arXiv abstract: 'integrate a thinking mode, enabling Gemma models to generate reasoning traces prior to responding'; abstract ranges '2.3B to 31B parameters'. Full text not fetched.
findings.implication_for_boar: The thinking-off quality claim is not in the abstract; the full PDF (not opened here) is the place to check whether Google reports E2B numbers with thinking disabled.

open_questions: Google's official launch blog post URL and exact date (secondary press says 2 April 2026; primary pages show July 2026 dates). Not found in search.
Whether Google's model card reports E2B benchmark numbers with thinking off, and how they compare to thinking on. Not in the fetched card text; the full tech report PDF was not opened.

Exact behaviour of the llama.cpp chat template for E2B: whether the enable_thinking kwarg or --reasoning off removes <|think|> and whether the empty/absent thought block parses correctly in b11010. Not verified here; needs a run on the mini.
Whether Google publishes an official QAT GGUF (not only the unquantized QAT checkpoint); no Google-owned QAT GGUF was found.
Licence NOTICE or Gemma-specific use policy attached to Apache-2.0 weights: not checked beyond the metadata field.
Whether the 2.3B/5.1B figures are the same counting convention used for Qwen3-1.7B, so the size comparison is fair. Not verified.

sweeps.angle: Google's own mobile path for Gemma 4 E2B: LiteRT / LiteRT-LM / AI Edge, backends, published per-device numbers, file formats and sizes, memory, licence, RN/Kotlin integration, and the Google AI Edge Gallery app, compared with llama.cpp on CPU.

findings.claim: Google's LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 page lists only E2B and E4B as supported LiteRT-LM sizes; larger models are 'coming soon'. E2B file is gemma-4-E2B-it.litertlm, 2.58 GB; E4B is 3.65 GB. The page was last updated 2026-09-04 UTC.
findings.evidence: Fetched developers.google.com/edge/litert-lm/models/gemma-4 (ai.google.dev URL 301-redirects there). Page states 'Last updated 2026-09-04 UTC'. Model files come from HF litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm and -E4B-it-litert-lm.
findings.implication_for_boar: The official LiteRT path for Gemma 4 E2B is a single .litertlm file of about 2.58 GB. That is the artifact a catalog entry would ship, not a GGUF. Any catalog entry for the maintainer must point to this format or to a llama.cpp GGUF, which is a separate artifact.

findings.claim: Google's published Gemma-4-E2B table has no Pixel or Tensor G3 row. The Android entry is a Samsung S26 Ultra: CPU 557 prefill / 47 decode tok/s, peak CPU memory 1733 MB; GPU 3808 prefill / 52 decode tok/s, 676 MB. Other rows: iPhone 17 Pro CPU 532/25, GPU 2878/56; Raspberry Pi 5 CPU 133/8.
findings.evidence: Table on the Google LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 page, columns: Platform (Device), Backend, Prefill tk/s, Decode tk/s, TTFT s, Peak CPU Memory MB. Benchmark setup is in the HF card: 1024 prefill tokens, 256 decode tokens, context 2048, CPU via XNNPACK with 4 threads.
findings.implication_for_boar: There is no published Google number for the Pixel 8a (Tensor G3). The S26 Ultra is a far faster chip than the 8a, so its 47-52 tok/s cannot be used as a Pixel 8a forecast. Our own measured 7.0-10.5 tok/s decode on the 8a is the only phone number we have, and it should be quoted as ours.

findings.claim: Google's May 2026 developer blog gives Gemma 4 E2B decode of 52 tok/s on Android GPU (OpenCL, S26 Ultra), 56 tok/s on iOS GPU (Metal, iPhone 17 Pro) and up to 76 tok/s on WebGPU (MacBook Pro). MTP gives up to 2.2x decode speedup on S26 Ultra GPU. On iOS CPU with XNNPACK weight caching, the ~2.58 GB model has a 607 MB physical footprint.
findings.evidence: Google Developers Blog, 'Blazing fast on-device GenAI with LiteRT-LM', dated May 19, 2026. The post does not state a licence.
findings.implication_for_boar: The 607 MB footprint is a claim about iOS CPU with XNNPACK weight caching. It is not a measurement on Android, so it does not prove that an 8 GB Android phone can run E2B with low RSS. It does support a memory-light design for the engine.

findings.claim: The LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 model card (HF litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm) reports Apache-2.0 licence, model size 2583 MB (2967 MB for the NPU variant), and a text-only weight footprint as low as 0.8 GB, with the 1.12 GB of embedding parameters memory-mapped.
findings.evidence: HF model card, opened 2026-10-21. The card says the embeddings are memory-mapped. It does not use the words 'per-layer embedding streaming' or 'PLE'. Benchmarks use XNNPACK with 4 threads, context 2048.
findings.implication_for_boar: Memory-mapping the embeddings is the closest official evidence that the runtime streams parts of the model from storage to cut RAM. This partly answers the PLE question. It is not proof of RAM savings on an 8 GB Android phone, so it needs a device test.
findings.source_date: unknown (card cites a speculative-decoding cutoff of 2026-05-05)

findings.claim: The HF model card says nothing about thinking mode or enable_thinking. The llama.cpp template problem we found (the model thinks by default) is therefore not documented in Google's LiteRT path.
findings.evidence: Card text checked for 'enable_thinking' and any thinking mode; neither appears. The card does mention a speculative-decoding (MTP) section for CPU and GPU.
findings.implication_for_boar: The enable_thinking:false fix is a llama.cpp-template fix. If the maintainer's app moves to LiteRT, the thinking behaviour must be checked on that runtime rather than assumed.

findings.claim: The LiteRT-LM repository is Apache-2.0. Kotlin Android API is stable, Python stable, C++ stable. iOS Swift and web JavaScript are early preview. Flutter is community-maintained. No React Native binding is listed. Gemma 4 support includes a v0.18.0 CLI example with MTP speculative decoding for E4B. GPU and NPU are named as the acceleration backends.
findings.evidence: Fetched github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT-LM. The release date for v0.18.0 was not visible in the fetched text.
findings.implication_for_boar: Our app is React Native (llama.rn), and the maintainer's app is native Kotlin. The Kotlin path is stable and the RN path has no official binding. A switch to LiteRT for BOAR would need a native-module bridge or a Kotlin-side engine, which is a substantial new integration before the 2026-10-23 freeze.

findings.claim: On Android the Kotlin dependency is com.google.ai.edge.litertlm:litertlm-android (one example pins 0.12.0). Initialization takes several seconds and should run off the main thread.
findings.evidence: Secondary community guide (gist, ashokvarmamatta). Not verified against the official Maven listing.
findings.implication_for_boar: Shows the Kotlin integration is simple to start. The version pin is unverified and must be checked against the Maven repository before use.

findings.claim: The HF card calls Android AI Core (Gemini Nano) 'the recommended path for production applications' on supported Android devices, and lists Gemma 4 as available through it. Whether E2B runs through AI Core on a Pixel 8a is not stated.
findings.evidence: HF litert-community card text, Android notes section. No device list is given.
findings.implication_for_boar: If AI Core serves Gemma 4 on the 8a, the maintainer could ship a system-managed model with no 2.6 GB file in the app. That is an open option that must be confirmed on the device before any decision.

findings.claim: A secondary Google AI Edge Gallery report says version 1.0.10 has an in-app benchmark screen (Models Management) that reports prefill and decode tok/s separately.
findings.evidence: Secondary articles (pasqualepillitteri.it and codersera.com). Not checked against the app's own release notes or the GitHub repository.
findings.implication_for_boar: If confirmed, the Gallery app gives a same-device, same-model benchmark that we can run on the 8a without writing code. This is a quick check of the Google-side number on our own hardware.

findings.claim: A community write-up on Gemma 4 E2B says many mid-range Qualcomm and MediaTek chips do not expose OpenCL to apps, and GPU initialisation can silently fall back to CPU. It reports 2-5 tok/s on CPU for mid-range phones.
findings.evidence: DEV Community article, 'Gemma 4 E2B on Mobile: Android vs iOS Reality'. Single author, no device list. Figures are unverified.
findings.implication_for_boar: A warning sign for the 8 GB class: the GPU backend may not be available, and CPU speed could be far below our 7-10 tok/s. This needs a device test on the 8a (Tensor G3 GPU/NPU support is not verified).

findings.claim: Community pages quote 142 tok/s and 1916 tok/s prefill for Gemma 4 on a Pixel 7 Pro. These appear to be for FunctionGemma 270M, not for Gemma 4 E2B, so they must not be used.
findings.evidence: Search-result snippets from secondary sites (noted as a model mix-up in the search summary). Not verified.
findings.implication_for_boar: Excluded from the decision. Shows that third-party speed numbers for Gemma 4 are unreliable.

findings.claim: Google's CPU numbers come from the LiteRT XNNPACK delegate. They are not llama.cpp numbers, so they do not compare directly with our llama.rn engine at b11010.
findings.evidence: HF card benchmark setup: 'CPU inference accelerated via the LiteRT XNNPACK delegate with 4 threads'. Google's table uses LiteRT-LM, not llama.cpp.
findings.implication_for_boar: A fair comparison with llama.cpp on CPU requires a same-device, same-model, same-quantisation test, which we have not run. Google's CPU row (47 decode on S26 Ultra) must not be read as llama.cpp speed.

open_questions: Does LiteRT-LM or AI Core run on Tensor G3 (Pixel 8a), and which backend (CPU, GPU or NPU) does the runtime pick there? No Google row exists for Pixel.
Do any independent Pixel 8a or Tensor G3 measurements of Gemma 4 E2B exist for LiteRT-LM or llama.cpp? Not found in this search.
Is there a React Native binding for LiteRT-LM? None is listed in the repo. Would the maintainer's native Kotlin app need a new engine to use LiteRT?
Does LiteRT-LM disable Gemma 4 thinking by default, or does it need a flag? The model card is silent.
What is the current LiteRT-LM release date and version (v0.18.0 is named but undated)?
What are the peak RSS and PSS numbers for E2B on 8 GB Android under LiteRT, comparable to our 4.5-4.6 GB PSS peak on llama.cpp?
Does the Google AI Edge Gallery app really ship a benchmark screen in v1.0.10 and which Gemma 4 variants does it load? Only secondary sources were found.
The licence of the Google Gemma 4 model weights themselves (Apache-2.0 on the HF card) should be checked against the official Gemma terms page, which was not opened here.

sweeps.angle: Angle 5: quality of Gemma 4 E2B for an offline research assistant with retrieval (benchmarks vs Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, Gemma 3n E2B; RAG grounding; factuality; thinking on/off; template and failure modes)

findings.claim: Google's own model card reports Gemma 4 E2B (instruction-tuned) at MMLU-Pro 60.0%, GPQA Diamond 43.4%, LiveCodeBench v6 44.0%, Tau2 24.5%, MMMU Pro 44.2%, MRCR v2 8-needle 128k 19.1%. It does not report IFEval, SimpleQA, plain MMLU, or HLE for E2B (HLE cells are empty).
findings.evidence: Fetched Google's Gemma 4 model card page (ai.google.dev model_card_4, page shows 'Last updated 2026-07-30'). The same numbers appear on the Hugging Face card google/gemma-4-E2B-it. Only comparison in the table is Gemma 3 27B. Qwen and Gemma 3n are not in the table. Secondary aggregators (BenchLM, DataLearner) give GPQA 40.5 without thinking and 43.3 with thinking, so the mode and harness behind 43.4 are not stated.
findings.source_date: 2026-07-30 (page update); model released ~April 2026 per Artificial Analysis
findings.implication_for_boar: Vendor-reported numbers only, with no stated harness. They cannot settle E2B vs Qwen3-1.7B on our task. Our own dev-set comparison (+0.03 utility, 2 seeds) remains the only like-for-like evidence, so the default-model decision rests on our measurement, not on the card.

findings.claim: Qwen3-1.7B's official report gives MMLU-Redux 73.9 / GPQA-Diamond 40.1 / IFEval strict 72.5 in thinking mode, and MMLU-Redux 64.4 / GPQA-Diamond 28.6 / IFEval strict 68.2 in non-thinking mode.
findings.evidence: Qwen3 Technical Report, Tables 19 and 20 (Qwen3-1.7B vs Qwen3-0.6B). Fetched the arXiv HTML v1, submitted 14 May 2025. The Qwen3-1.7B Hugging Face card contains no benchmark table and points to the report.
findings.implication_for_boar: This is the only published IFEval number for the Qwen 1.7B baseline. Gemma 4 E2B has no published IFEval, so instruction following for short cited answers cannot be compared on paper. Use our own format-compliance check (citation brackets, answer length).

findings.claim: Gemma 4 E2B's published thinking control is the <|think|> token in the system instruction. Thinking is off when the token is absent. When thinking is on, output is wrapped as <|channel>thought ... <channel|>. The card says larger models (not E2B or E4B) emit an empty thought block when thinking is disabled.
findings.evidence: Google model card (model_card_4): 'Thinking is turned on by including the <|think|> token at the start of the system prompt. Removing the token turns it off.' The prompt-formatting page says the 26B-A4B and 31B models 'may occasionally generate a thought channel even when thinking mode is explicitly turned off', and it does not describe this for E2B or E4B. The prompt-formatting fetch found nothing specific to E2B.
findings.implication_for_boar: The enable_thinking:false workaround fits Google's documented off-state for E2B. Still verify on the device that no <|channel>thought block leaks into the answer text, since the docs are silent for E2B.

findings.claim: llama.cpp exposes Gemma 4 thinking through a chat-template kwarg (--chat-template-kwargs with enable_thinking false), with llama-server recommended over llama-cli. One user report says enable_thinking=false and --reasoning off did not stop reasoning output in PocketPal and LM Studio.
findings.evidence: Unsloth Gemma 4 run guide recommends llama-server with enable_thinking:false via chat-template kwargs. PocketPal issue #677 reports the flag does not suppress reasoning and that LM Studio with the same GGUF behaves the same. That is one user report, not confirmed as a llama.cpp bug, and the issue date was not read.
findings.source_date: undated (fetched 2026-10-21); PocketPal issue date not verified
findings.implication_for_boar: Our fix depends on the template-kwarg path being honoured at the pinned llama.cpp commit b11010, and on the app's wrapper passing it. The lab check: run one prompt through the shipped GGUF with the kwarg and grep for the thought channel, before the maintainer ships the catalog entry.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 E2B's bundled chat template re-injects prior-turn reasoning in multi-turn tool-calling, which can cause verbatim repetition loops with llama.cpp --jinja. Single-turn chat is reported unaffected. No official fix is merged on the model page.
findings.evidence: Hugging Face discussion #36 on google/gemma-4-E2B-it, opened 10 Jun by a third party. The author reproduced loops on a pruned-MoE derivative (4/12 seeds with the stock template, 0 with the fix). Severity on E2B was not measured. A corrected template is linked from the author's own GGUF repo.
findings.implication_for_boar: Not on our path if the app is single-turn RAG with no tool-call history. Confirm that the chat path never sends reasoning_content back on assistant turns, and that the GGUF template is the one we tested.

findings.claim: The only E2B-specific RAG faithfulness number found: in an ESG RAG benchmark, Gemma 4 E2B scored faithfulness 0.784, factual correctness 0.423 and answer relevancy 0.760 (lowest of the set). The judge and dataset generator were Qwen3-family, which the authors flag as a bias risk.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2609.15242, 'Empirical Evaluation of Open-Source LLMs for RAG in ESG Domain'. Seen in search results only; the paper was not opened, so the table and judge details are unverified beyond the snippet.
findings.implication_for_boar: Suggests E2B grounds reasonably under RAG, but it is one domain, one judge family, and weak answer relevancy. Our own RAG faithfulness test (citation accuracy, unsupported-claim rate on our corpus) is still needed before the default switch.

findings.claim: On-device medical RAG study: Gemma 4 (a 4B-class model, not E2B) was about 2x more faithful than Gemma 3n and grounded about as well as a 397B Qwen model.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2606.29580 (MAM-AI), evaluated with a Lynx-70B judge then gpt-5. Seen in search results only; the paper was not opened. The 4B size is taken from the snippet, not verified.
findings.implication_for_boar: Supports the direction (Gemma 4 grounds better than Gemma 3n) but is not an E2B number and uses an external judge. Do not quote as E2B evidence.

findings.claim: Google's own card lists factual accuracy and task limits for all Gemma 4 models: outputs may be incorrect or outdated, the model is not a knowledge base, and performance is strongest with clear prompts.
findings.evidence: Known Limitations section of model_card_4: 'Factual accuracy: Outputs may be incorrect or outdated, since the model is not a knowledge base.' and 'Task complexity: Performance is strongest with clear prompts.' Not specific to E2B.
findings.implication_for_boar: Supports the design thesis that retrieval must supply facts and the answer must cite them. It also means no SimpleQA-style closed-book number should be expected to be high for a 2.3B-effective model.

findings.claim: Gemma 3n E2B (the previous generation) has an official IT card with MMLU 60.1, MMLU-Pro 40.5, GPQA Diamond 24.8, HumanEval 66.5, and no IFEval, SimpleQA or TruthfulQA entries.
findings.evidence: Gemma 3n model card page on ai.google.dev. The card is marked deprecated and dated 2025-06-17 (page revision, not release). The MMLU-Pro 40.5 for 3n vs 60.0 for Gemma 4 E2B are from different cards and versions, so the jump is not like-for-like.
findings.implication_for_boar: Gemma 4 E2B is claimed to be a large knowledge and reasoning step up over 3n. Our preference for E2B over Qwen3-1.7B is about refusals, grounding and citations, not raw benchmark strength.

findings.claim: Artificial Analysis lists Gemma 4 E2B as an estimate (independent evaluation forthcoming): Intelligence Index 8 for the reasoning variant and 6 for non-reasoning, ranked #64 of 141 in its size class. Qwen3 1.7B, Qwen3 4B and Gemma 3n E2B are not on the page. An earlier search snippet gave reasoning 10, so the value is not stable.
findings.evidence: Fetched artificialanalysis.ai/models/releases/gemma-4-e2b. The page marks the score as an estimate. The AA-Omniscience accuracy and hallucination-rate fields are named but show no E2B values.
findings.implication_for_boar: No independent index value for a head-to-head with Qwen3-1.7B yet. Re-check before the 10-31 decision, since an independent score may be published.

findings.claim: GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro figures for Gemma 4 E2B differ across aggregators (GPQA 40.5 without thinking and 43.3 with, from DataLearner; 43.4 from BenchLM; MMLU-Pro 60 in thinking mode). Aggregator coverage is partial (BenchLM says 6 verified scores out of 125 tracked).
findings.evidence: DataLearner E2B analysis page (search snippet) and BenchLM E2B page (search snippet). Not opened in full.
findings.implication_for_boar: Quote only the Google card value and say which mode it is, never an aggregator number as a fact.

findings.claim: The Gemma 4 technical report (arXiv 2607.02770, submitted 2 July 2026, revised 24 July 2026) covers the 2.3B to 31B suite, with thinking traces and E2B tables, but the fetched abstract page had no E2B numbers.
findings.evidence: arXiv abstract fetch. The full PDF or HTML v2 was not read, so SimpleQA, IFEval, hallucination and thinking-vs-non-thinking tables for E2B remain unchecked.
findings.implication_for_boar: The most likely place for the missing E2B factuality and thinking-delta numbers. Reading it is the cheapest next step for this angle.

open_questions: No published IFEval or SimpleQA number for Gemma 4 E2B found on Google's card, the HF card, or aggregators. Read arXiv 2607.02770 PDF or HTML v2 for those tables.
No like-for-like Gemma 4 E2B vs Qwen3-1.7B benchmark exists in the sources read. The baseline comparison must come from our own harness on the same items.
Thinking-on vs thinking-off delta for E2B is not published in the sources read; the card gives only the instruct table.
Refusal and over-refusal rate for E2B vs Qwen3-1.7B: no source found. Our dev-set claim that E2B refuses less is internal and unverified externally.
Citation and quoting behaviour under retrieval for E2B: no external source found; our measured citation retention is the only evidence.
Date confusion and verbosity/repetition failure modes for E2B at short answer lengths: no source found beyond the template loop report.
Whether the llama.cpp template kwarg enable_thinking works at the pinned commit b11010 for E2B specifically: needs a check against the commit or PR history, not only the PocketPal report.
Qwen3-1.7B official SimpleQA or factuality figures were not in the report text read (first 100k characters only); the rest was not read.
Tool-calling malformation under long context and the LiteRT Mali GPU report were seen in search snippets only and were not opened, so they are not listed as findings.

sweeps.angle: Angle 4: measured on-device performance of Gemma 4 E2B (and E4B for contrast) on phones, by device, runtime and quantization, with thermal notes. Web research only, nothing downloaded or run.

findings.claim: Google's LiteRT-LM table for Gemma-4-E2B (2.58 GB) reports on Samsung S26 Ultra (Android): CPU prefill 557 tok/s, decode 47 tok/s, TTFT 1.8 s, peak CPU mem 1733 MB; GPU prefill 3808, decode 52, TTFT 0.3 s, mem 676 MB.
findings.evidence: Table on developers.google.com/edge/litert-lm/models/gemma-4 (opened 2026-10-21; page 'Last updated 2026-09-04 UTC'). The page gives no prefill/decode token counts, context length, thread count, or whether MTP was enabled for these rows. Vendor-run, not independently reproduced.
findings.implication_for_boar: This is the only official Android E2B decode figure, and it is a flagship Snapdragon device on LiteRT, not llama.cpp GGUF on a Tensor G3. It cannot be used as a Pixel 8a expectation. Our measured 10.5 tok/s short and 7.0 tok/s over 13 min (Pixel 8a) is roughly 5-6x lower; the gap is plausibly chip plus runtime, but that split is unconfirmed.

findings.claim: Same Google table, Gemma-4-E4B (3.65 GB) on S26 Ultra: CPU decode 18 tok/s (prefill 195, TTFT 5.3 s, mem 3283 MB); GPU decode 22 tok/s (prefill 1293, TTFT 0.8 s, mem 710 MB). E2B is about 2.6x faster than E4B on the same CPU.
findings.evidence: Same page, E4B table. Google's own InfoQ-cited claim (finding 6) says E2B runs about three times as fast as E4B.
findings.implication_for_boar: The speed case for E2B over E4B is consistent across vendor tables. E4B on the CPU is only 18 tok/s even on flagship hardware, which supports keeping E4B out of the 8 GB default.

findings.claim: Google's MTP (multi-token prediction) is stated to give up to 2.2x decode on mobile GPU and up to 1.5x on mobile CPU. It is recommended for all tasks on GPU and for E4B on CPU. For E2B on CPU, it helps rewrite, summarize and coding, but may slow freeform or generative prompts.
findings.evidence: Notes section of the Google LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 page. The tables do not say whether MTP was on in the rows above.
findings.implication_for_boar: BOAR answers are generative, so the vendor itself warns that MTP on E2B CPU may hurt. The speed number for the device plan depends on whether MTP is on, and the quality or speed trade has to be measured on our own set before the catalog entry ships.

findings.claim: No Pixel or Tensor G3/G4 rows and no phone NPU rows appear in Google's Gemma 4 LiteRT-LM performance table. Listed devices are S26 Ultra, iPhone 17 Pro, Linux/RTX 4090, MacBook Pro M4 and M4 Max, Windows LunarLake, and Raspberry Pi 5.
findings.evidence: Full table on the same page, opened 2026-10-21. Searches for 'Gemma 4 E2B Pixel 8 Tensor G3 tokens/sec' returned nothing measured for Pixel 8, 8a, or Tensor G3.
findings.implication_for_boar: There is no external measurement for the target class (Pixel 8a, Tensor G3, 8 GB). Our own Pixel 8a run is the only Tensor G3 data point, so the decision rests on our measurement, not on an external reference.

findings.claim: Google's table lists Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB CPU at E2B decode 8 tok/s (prefill 133, TTFT 7.8 s, mem 1546 MB) and E4B decode 3 tok/s.
findings.evidence: Same LiteRT-LM page, IoT row. Used only as a sanity range: the Pi 5 is a much weaker CPU than a Tensor G3 under a sustained load, so this does not predict the Pixel 8a.
findings.implication_for_boar: Our Pixel 8a 7-10.5 tok/s sits between the Pi 5 and flagship numbers. It is consistent with a mid-tier CPU and is not evidence of a runtime bug.

findings.claim: InfoQ (2026-04-13) reports Google's Gemma 4 launch positioning: E2B needs 8 GB RAM and about 2 GB disk; E4B needs 12 GB RAM and about 4 GB disk; the 26B MoE needs 24 GB RAM. Google claims up to 4x faster than prior versions, about 60% less battery use, and E2B about 3x faster than E4B. The article gives no device-level tok/s.
findings.evidence: Opened infoq.com/news/2026/04/gemma-4-android-ai-inference. Article names AICore Developer Preview as the Android route, and Ollama and LM Studio as desktop routes.
findings.implication_for_boar: The vendor-stated RAM floor puts E4B above an 8 GB phone (12 GB) while E2B is at 8 GB. That supports E2B as the 8 GB model, but it is a secondary report of Google's stated requirements, not a measurement.

findings.claim: Community dev.to hands-on figures (reported via gemma4all.com, 2026-07-11) give Gemma 4 E2B at about 12-18 tok/s on iPhone with Metal, and about 12-20 tok/s on a recent Snapdragon flagship. E4B is about 10-15 tok/s on iPhone 15 Pro or 16 Pro and 8-15 tok/s on a Snapdragon flagship. No phone model names carry their own numbers.
findings.evidence: Opened gemma4all.com/blog/gemma-4-on-phone. Figures are per device class, not per device, and no prefill, temperature or duration is given.
findings.implication_for_boar: Secondary and unnamed. It suggests phone E2B in the low tens of tok/s on flagships, so our 7-10.5 on Pixel 8a is a plausible mid-tier figure. It does not establish a Pixel 8a number.

findings.claim: The same gemma4all page says that on Android E2B fits 8 GB+ devices; 4-6 GB budget phones are a maybe for E2B and a no for E4B. It cites Q4_K_M GGUF sizes of about 1.3 GB for E2B and 2.5 GB for E4B (community/Off Grid figures), and says Google's in-app LiteRT builds need under 1.5 GB runtime RAM for E2B on some devices.
findings.evidence: Opened gemma4all.com/blog/gemma-4-on-phone. Sizes and RAM tiers are community or spec claims with no measurement method. The page says the Android RAM spread varies more by SKU.
findings.implication_for_boar: The GGUF file is smaller than our 3.11 GB LiteRT file, so the RSS we measure (4.5-4.6 GB peak PSS) is mostly runtime and KV overhead, not weights. Confirming this needs our own measurement.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 thinks by default in llama.cpp chat templates: thinking is turned on by a <|think|> token in the system prompt, and disabling needs --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' on llama-server. Output is wrapped in <|channel>thought ... <channel|>, and larger models may still emit an empty thought block with thinking disabled.
findings.evidence: Opened the Unsloth Gemma 4 guide (markdown version). Unsloth says llama-cli may not work reliably for the disable flag. A third-party extension doc says --reasoning off and --no-jinja are the only flags that make thinking impossible, and that --reasoning-budget 0 only cuts the thought block short. That claim is unverified against llama.cpp source.
findings.implication_for_boar: Supports our enable_thinking:false fix. Note that the flag is a template kwarg, so it must reach the app's llama.cpp chat template path; a missing flag would silently return thought blocks and cost decode time. Verify on device that the thought block is absent and that E2B does not emit an empty one.

findings.claim: LM Studio's Gemma 4 E2B metadata shows 'Enable Thinking' defaulting to true, with reasoning parsing on <|channel>thought and <channel|>. A Hugging Face discussion reports the Jinja workaround works on 26B but returns only blank lines on 31B under LM Studio 4.9.1 (macOS).
findings.evidence: Search result snippets from lmstudio.ai/google/gemma-4-e2b and the unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF HF discussion #6. Not opened in full.
findings.implication_for_boar: Shows that thinking-on is the default in several runtimes, not only ours. The blank-output report is a warning to test the flag on every model variant we ship.

findings.claim: Gemma 3n E4B on a Pixel 6 Pro reportedly ran at about 4.4 tok/s decode for an image prompt and over 6 tok/s for text chat, from a single Hacker News comment. A second commenter reported Gemma 3n E2B (int4) on a Pixel 4a taking over 10 minutes for a slow image task, with no tok/s figure.
findings.evidence: Search result summary citing hn.nuxt.dev/item/44044199 (HN mirror; not opened). Single anonymous user reports, undated (likely mid-2025). Different model generation and chip.
findings.implication_for_boar: Gives an older-generation reference for Google phone models on a mid-tier SoC. Not a Gemma 4 or Tensor G3 number, so it cannot replace our Pixel 8a data.

findings.claim: Sustained-performance evidence on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 is indirect: Android Authority reported that a Qualcomm reference device halved its performance in a 3DMark Wildlife Stress Test. This is a graphics workload, not LLM decode, and the article cautions that retail devices may differ.
findings.evidence: Search snippet from androidauthority.com/snapdragon-8-gen-3-benchmarks-3379534; not opened in full.
findings.implication_for_boar: Shows that a sustained-load halving is plausible on flagship SoCs, which argues for multi-minute runs in our acceptance tests. It does not measure E2B.

findings.claim: No public measurement was found of Gemma 4 E2B or E4B sustained decode with temperature or clock data on any Android phone. The only thermal report found is one anecdote: E2B on an iPhone 15 slowed after roughly a couple thousand tokens (thermal), while a Pixel 9 Pro kept going.
findings.evidence: Search results on LocalLLaMA and aggregator threads (opened search summaries only). The anecdote has no stable URL I could cite and is undated, so it is recorded here as unverified rather than as a source.
findings.implication_for_boar: Our own 13-minute run with thermal status 1 is the only sustained Gemma 4 E2B data on an 8 GB Android class phone. A 2-3x decline from burst to sustained decode is possible but unmeasured in the external literature. Keep the sustained run as the basis for the claim.

findings.claim: Google's MTP and default runtime settings mean the LiteRT numbers are not directly comparable to a llama.cpp GGUF Q4_K_M run; the page gives no quantization for its rows beyond the file size.
findings.evidence: LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 page (2026-09-04) lists model size only, not quantization, for the table rows. Community GGUF Q4_K_M sizes are from gemma4all.com (2026-07-11).
findings.implication_for_boar: Any comparison between the S26 numbers and our Pixel 8a numbers must state runtime, quantization and MTP state. A same-runtime comparison (llama.cpp vs llama.cpp on the Pixel 8a) is the only one that answers the default-model question.

open_questions: Measured Gemma 4 E2B decode/prefill/RSS on Pixel 8, 8a, 8 Pro or 9 (Tensor G3/G4) with llama.cpp GGUF Q4_K_M: none found. Needs a community or own run.
Same-device, same-runtime comparison of Gemma 4 E2B vs Qwen3-1.7B vs Qwen3-4B vs Gemma 3n E2B on an 8 GB phone (tok/s, TTFT, RSS, thermal): none found.
Whether Google's table rows used MTP on or off; whether MTP on E2B CPU slows our generative answers on Tensor G3.

Exact benchmark conditions for the LiteRT rows (prefill and decode token counts, context length, threads). The search summary cites a 1024 prefill / 256 decode / 2048 context / 4-thread setup from the Hugging Face model card, but that card was not opened, so it remains unverified.
Sustained decode on Android for E2B over 10+ minutes with temperature and clock logs: none found. The iPhone 15 throttling anecdote has no stable source.
Whether llama.cpp at b11010 (our pinned commit) has any Gemma 4 E2B fixes, perf issues or thinking-template regressions. Not checked against the llama.cpp GitHub issue tracker in this pass.
Size of the E2B LiteRT vs GGUF Q4_K_M RSS difference (our 4.5-4.6 GB PSS peak vs community ~1.3 GB file): not separated by any source.
Whether the 12 GB RAM figure for E4B from the InfoQ/Google positioning is a hard floor or a recommendation; affects whether E4B can be run at all on 8 GB phones with the app's other memory.

sweeps.angle: Angle 3: llama.cpp and llama.rn support for Gemma 4 (gemma4 arch), fixes after b11010 that matter for mobile, thinking/template handling, open issues, build and PLE questions

findings.claim: Our pinned llama.cpp tag b11010 was published 2026-09-17, and its release notes list no Gemma 4 changes (only an unrelated Vulkan fix #28975).
findings.evidence: GitHub release page for tag b11010 says published 17 September (year shown as 2026 in footer); the notes mention only 'vulkan: work around NV bug with argsort_large.comp' (#28975) as a change.
findings.implication_for_boar: The pin is recent enough to contain the Gemma 4 work merged in April 2026, but the release notes do not confirm which Gemma 4 fixes it carries. Gemma 4 behaviour must be checked on the pinned build itself, not assumed from the release notes.

findings.claim: llama.rn 0.13.0-rc.4 (2026-09-17) synced llama.cpp to b10951 and b11010. The newest stable llama.rn we found is 0.12.9 (2026-08-04), synced to b10256. The 0.13 line is still pre-release.
findings.evidence: llama.rn releases page changelog table: 0.13.0-rc.4 dated 2026-09-17 'synced to b10951 and b11010, plus a vendor sync'; 0.13.0-rc.7 dated 2026-10-05 synced to b11366 (and a separate change targets b11385); 0.12.9 dated 2026-08-04 synced to b10256. 0.12.9 is marked Latest.
findings.implication_for_boar: Shipping on the stable 0.12.9 line would mean a llama.cpp build older than b11010; that build's Gemma 4 support is unverified. Either pin the rc line or verify gemma4 against the exact llama.cpp commit in the chosen llama.rn version. The maintainer's native Kotlin app is a separate path and needs its own check.

findings.claim: llama.rn release notes never mention Gemma 4 or gemma4 in any release from 0.12.8 to 0.13.0-rc.7.
findings.evidence: The first 10 entries of the llama.rn releases page, back to 0.12.8 (2026-07-28), contain no Gemma 4 mention; the wording is limited to llama.cpp sync lines.
findings.implication_for_boar: There is no llama.rn-level Gemma 4 fix to point to; support rests on the underlying llama.cpp commit. Our own test on the pinned build is the only confirmation of the gemma4 path.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 support already had follow-up merges in llama.cpp in early April 2026. PR #21277 (kv-cache: do not quantize SWA KV cache) and #21326 (Gemma 4 template parser fixes) were both merged 2026-04-02. The original gemma4 architecture PR was not identified.
findings.evidence: Merged-PR list from the llama.cpp PR search (sorted by merge date): #21277 merged Apr 2 2026, #21326 'Gemma 4 template parser fixes' merged Apr 2 2026. Gemma 4 release date given by several sources as April 2 2026. The architecture PR itself is on a page of results not reached.
findings.implication_for_boar: Gemma 4 landed in llama.cpp in the same week as the model release, so b11010 (September) is well past it. Finding the exact architecture PR number remains open.

findings.claim: Google's llama.cpp integration page covers Gemma 4 with GGUF repo ggml-org/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF and llama-server -hf, but says nothing about thinking or reasoning flags or recommended sampling. The page is marked deprecated and points to a new site.
findings.evidence: Page content: model repo ggml-org/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF, llama-cli -hf and llama-server -hf on port 8080 with /v1; no mention of thinking, reasoning or enable_thinking; 'Last updated 2026-04-16 UTC'; deprecation notice pointing to gemma.ai.
findings.implication_for_boar: Google's own llama.cpp doc does not cover the thinking default. The app's enable_thinking:false choice is not documented by the vendor and must be justified by our own measurements.

findings.claim: Thinking default regression: a llama.cpp build after 2026-04-10 (commit d7ff074) registers Gemma 4 thinking tags, which activates the reasoning-budget sampler with a default of 2147483647 tokens. Reported symptoms: unbounded thinking, hangs, KV cache growth into RAM/swap, and llama-server crashes on memory-limited systems.
findings.evidence: Forge issue #54 (opened 2026-04-13, closed completed 2026-04-28): Gemma 4 31B took 340 s versus 100 s with --reasoning-budget 0 at similar quality; the author changed the server default to --reasoning-budget 0 for all models.
findings.implication_for_boar: On the pinned build, runaway thinking is a real risk. enable_thinking:false may or may not disable the budget sampler path; this must be tested directly (unbounded token count and memory growth with thinking off). Passing --reasoning-budget 0 as an extra guard is a cheap safety step to include in the catalog entry.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 chat-template reasoning output is handled inconsistently across frontends. Upstream llama.cpp maps channel tags to reasoning_content via a peg-gemma4 template; KoboldCpp frontends can show raw channel tags that break streaming.
findings.evidence: Secondary aggregation of a KoboldCpp issue (LostRuins/koboldcpp#2092) and llama.cpp template discussions; the claim is from a search summary, not an opened primary page.
findings.implication_for_boar: If our native Kotlin app or the bench app parses channel tokens itself, it may leak them into visible answers. Check the answer text for the thought channel marker in the pinned build when enable_thinking is false.

findings.claim: llama.cpp PR #29115 'chat : fix gemma4 required tool grammar' was merged 2026-09-19 as f072b10, after b11010. It fixes tool calls going unconstrained under tool_choice=required (issue #29089). It does not show an effect on plain chat.
findings.evidence: PR page: opened by aldehir, merged to master 2026-09-19, reviewed by pwilkin and jhen0409; the change is limited to the grammar for required tool calls.
findings.implication_for_boar: Not in b11010. Only matters if the app uses required tool calls; our current answer path does not need it.

findings.claim: Open PR #30722 (opened 2026-10-17, unmerged) gates the thought channel in JSON-schema grammars on enable_thinking. Without it, Gemma 4 E2B/E4B can emit reasoning before the JSON and exhaust the work budget (finish_reason length). The E2B/E4B templates do not add an empty thought block, unlike the larger Gemma 4 templates.
findings.evidence: PR page: fixes issue #30256; tests added in tests/test-chat.cpp; at least two approvals required; reporter says the PR removes reasoning on E2B while keeping the thinking path working.
findings.implication_for_boar: If the catalog entry or app uses json_schema output with enable_thinking false on E2B, this is a live hazard on b11010 that is not fixed yet. Test before relying on JSON mode.

findings.claim: Post-b11010 Gemma 4 commits that touch mobile-relevant code paths are few: #30266 (2026-10-11) improves OpenCL flash attention and allows dk512 for Gemma 4 (GPU path, Adreno/Mali relevant), #30882 (2026-10-20) fixes Gemma 4 FFN activation in the mtmd (vision/audio) path. The CPU text path has no Gemma 4 fix in this window.
findings.evidence: Merged-PR list filtered for gemma4 / gemma-4 titles: #30266 merged Oct 11 2026 'opencl: improve fa, allow dk512 for gemma-4, improve dk64'; #30882 merged Oct 20 2026 'mtmd: fix gemma 4 ffn act'. Other Gemma 4 items in the window were CUDA-only (#29152) or DSpark drafts (#29226).
findings.implication_for_boar: Moving from b11010 to a newer build gains little for the CPU text path on 8 GB phones, unless we use vision. Those commits are relevant only if the app uses GPU/OpenCL or image input.

findings.claim: Google's LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 page reports E2B on a Galaxy S26 Ultra at about 47 tok/s decode (CPU) and 52 (GPU), with peak CPU memory 1,733 MB (CPU) and 676 MB (GPU). Our Pixel 8a measurement on llama.cpp (7.0-10.5 tok/s decode, PSS 4.5-4.6 GB) is well below that. This comparison is across a different runtime and device.
findings.evidence: Search snippet quoting the LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 table (Galaxy S26 Ultra row); the page itself was not fetched, so the numbers are from the snippet. Third-party Pixel 9 Pro estimates (10-25 tok/s) conflict with each other and are uncited.
findings.implication_for_boar: Our llama.cpp numbers are probably not the ceiling for this model on this class of phone; the gap may be runtime or device (Tensor G3 vs Snapdragon 8 Elite). Before the decision, fetch the LiteRT-LM page directly and check whether its numbers come from a comparable build, so the maintainer does not expect LiteRT-level speed from llama.cpp.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 E2B has 2.3B effective parameters (5.1B with Per-Layer Embeddings), 35 layers, and 128K context, and it is Apache 2.0 licensed. E4B has 4.5B effective (8B with embeddings) and 42 layers.
findings.evidence: Multiple secondary summaries (apxml, Amazon Bedrock model card, a Gemma 4 overview article) agree on 2.3B effective / 5.1B with PLE for E2B; one outlier site with garbled text gives different numbers and was rejected.
findings.implication_for_boar: The PLE tensors are a large share of the 3.11 GB file. Their memory placement (mmap versus anonymous allocation) decides how much of the 4.5 GB PSS is the model; that question is unanswered (see open questions).

findings.claim: No public source found on whether llama.cpp memory-maps Gemma 4 PLE tensors on Android, nor on PLE-related slow prefill or KV cache issues specific to gemma4 in llama.cpp.
findings.evidence: Searches for PLE mmap, PLE slow, and Pixel per-layer embedding memory returned only model-card background and LiteRT-LM figures; no llama.cpp issue or PR found on this topic.
findings.implication_for_boar: The 4.5 GB PSS and the thermal and speed drop cannot be explained from public sources. Profile the PLE tensors on the device (mmap on, off, or lazy) before choosing the default.

findings.claim: Two HF GGUF repos (ggml-org/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF) show only a loading error and a BOS-token question in discussions; no reports of speed, memory, thinking or quality issues. Gemma 4 E2B has an MTP drafter GGUF on HF and a WIP llama.cpp PR (#23398) for MTP, which is not merged.
findings.evidence: HF discussions page lists 2 entries: an Ollama loading error (#2) and 'why is add_bos_token = false?' (#1), both relative dates ('7 months ago'). PR #23398 described in a search summary as work in progress.
findings.implication_for_boar: The GGUF repo itself has no recorded quality problem; the absence of reports is weak evidence. MTP speculative decoding is not an option for the default in this window.

findings.claim: A Google AI developer forum thread reports repetitive looping in Gemma 4 thinking output. Commenters suspected 4-bit quantization and suggested lower temperature or top-k changes. The poster said temperature alone did not fix it. No llama.cpp issue was found for it.
findings.evidence: discuss.ai.google.dev thread 'Gemma4: How to prevent looping output in thinking?' (undated in the snippet); the claim is from the search summary and was not opened.
findings.implication_for_boar: Looping is a known community risk with thinking on; keep a max-token cap in the app and test looping with thinking off on our dev set.

open_questions: Exact number and date of the original llama.cpp gemma4 architecture PR (not found; search results only showed April 2 follow-ups).

Does the pinned b11010 include commit d7ff074 (the thinking-tag registration that activates the budget sampler)? Does enable_thinking:false fully bypass the reasoning-budget sampler on b11010? Needs a direct test.
Which llama.rn version (0.13.0-rc.4 or later) bundles b11010 in a release that our React Native bench app uses, and what the stable 0.12.9 line (synced to b10256) lacks for gemma4.
Android build flags (dotprod, i8mm, SME) and their measured effect on E2B decode and prefill on Tensor G3 / Pixel 8a. Not researched; no source opened.
Whether llama.cpp memory-maps PLE tensors on Android and how much of the 4.5 GB PSS they account for; no public source.
Quality gap between llama.cpp GGUF and the reference implementation for Gemma 4 E2B. No source with a measured comparison was found.
Whether the Google LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 numbers (47 tok/s decode on S26 Ultra) are comparable to llama.cpp; the page was not opened.
Exact release date and content of llama.cpp PR #28335 'model, mtmd: fix gemma4 vision handling', seen only in a search summary.

sweeps.angle: Angle 6: memory on 8 GB Android for Gemma 4 E2B (why RSS is ~4.5 GB for a ~3.1 GB Q4_K_M file; PLE caching; mmap vs mlock; KV cache and context; Q3/Q2/IQ3 quality vs size; QAT checkpoint size; text-only files; Android LMK and per-app memory limits)

findings.claim: Google's LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 E2B card: the 2.58 GB model file = 0.79 GB text decoder weights + 1.12 GB embedding parameters. LiteRT keeps main weights resident and memory-maps the embedding parameters; vision and audio models load on demand. Measured CPU memory on S26 Ultra (Android, CPU backend) = 1733 MB, decode 46.9 tok/s, prefill 557 tok/s, 2048 ctx, 4 threads; CPU memory measured with rusage::ru_maxrss.
findings.evidence: Table and quoted memory text from the model card mirror. Same card: Linux Arm CPU 1628 MB; iPhone 17 Pro CPU 607 MB; Raspberry Pi 5 CPU 1546 MB. Mirror, not the primary Google/LiteRT repo; no date shown on the page.
findings.source_date: undated (mirror of LiteRT-LM card; collection-level metadata only)
findings.implication_for_boar: On a different engine, the whole Gemma 4 E2B working set is ~1.7 GB CPU memory on a flagship Android, versus our ~4.5 GB PSS on a Pixel 8a with llama.cpp GGUF. The gap is engine/layout-specific, not inherent to the model file size. Do not quote the LiteRT number as a llama.cpp number.

findings.claim: Gemma 3n E2B docs (note: 3n, not Gemma 4): Per-Layer Embedding (PLE) data can be generated outside the model's operating memory and cached to fast local storage; standard execution loads over 5B parameters; with PLE caching and parameter skipping the effective memory load is 1.91B parameters.
findings.evidence: Quoted from the Gemma 3n model overview: 'The PLE data can be generated separately, outside the operating memory of the model, cached to fast storage' and 'an effective memory load of just under 2 billion (1.91B) parameters'. Page 'last updated 2025-11-01 UTC'.
findings.implication_for_boar: The documented lever for PLE is storage caching (not mlock). Whether llama.cpp b11010 implements PLE caching for Gemma 4 is NOT confirmed by any source found; an engine-side PLE cache would be a patch, not a flag, and must be measured on-device before it affects the default-model decision.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 E2B architecture (Google model card): 2.3B effective parameters, 5.1B including embeddings, 35 layers, 128K context; per-layer embeddings give each decoder layer its own small per-token embedding table that is large but used only for lookups; vision encoder ~150M, audio encoder ~300M params.
findings.evidence: Fetched model card page: 'E2B has 2.3B effective parameters, or 5.1B including embeddings, across 35 layers'; 'The small models feature a 128K context window'; per-layer embeddings described as above. Google's card gives no RAM figure for E2B.
findings.implication_for_boar: The 5.1B vs 2.3B split explains why file size (3.1 GB) is much larger than the compute-active parameters; the embedding tables are the part that can be mapped instead of resident. Google publishes no official RAM number, so any RSS budget must come from our own measurements.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 E2B attention layout: 512-token sliding window on local layers, interleaved with full global attention, final layer always global; global layers use unified Keys and Values and Proportional RoPE to reduce long-context memory.
findings.evidence: Fetched Google Gemma 4 E2B HF model card (google/gemma-4-E2B-it): 'E2B uses a 512-token sliding window'; global layers use unified K/V and p-RoPE. The card gives no per-layer KV head counts, so the exact KV byte size at 4096 ctx is not confirmed here.
findings.source_date: undated page; collection updated ~21 days before fetch (approx. early Oct 2026, unverified)
findings.implication_for_boar: KV cache should be much smaller than a full-attention model of the same size. Setting ctx to 4096 is therefore a modest lever; the 4.5 GB PSS is more likely dominated by weights mapped as file pages plus compute buffers than by KV. Needs a measured split (weights vs KV vs compute) on the Pixel 8a before claiming it.

findings.claim: Unsloth's Gemma 4 QAT page lists E2B file sizes: QAT int4 UD-Q4_K_XL 2.62 GB; naive Q4_0 from the QAT checkpoint 3.35 GB; mobile mixture UD-Q2_K_XL 2.19 GB; BF16 reference 9.31 GB. Same page: QAT int4 uses '~72% less memory' than the original with near-original accuracy, and claims E2B 'runs on 3GB RAM' (total RAM+VRAM, assuming ~8K context).
findings.evidence: Fetched table and the intro/hardware table from unsloth.ai/docs/models/gemma-4/qat. The 3 GB RAM and 72% figures are vendor claims from Unsloth, not measured by us and not Google's numbers; no mmap or PLE discussion on the page.
findings.implication_for_boar: A QAT UD-Q4_K_XL GGUF at 2.62 GB is ~0.5 GB smaller than the current 3.11 GB Q4_K_M and could be a direct memory lever with similar quality class. It is a candidate to measure on the Pixel 8a before any default switch. It is not verified as lower RSS.

findings.claim: Google's QAT checkpoint size and the '72%' figure could not be confirmed from Google's own announcement: the Google Developers Blog URL returned 404 and the Android Authority article returned 403. Secondary coverage repeats 72% and a '~1 GB E2B' figure without a primary source.
findings.evidence: WebFetch of developers.googleblog.com URL returned 404; androidauthority.com returned 403. Search snippets from gmagazine and wikidocs repeat 72% and ~1 GB; not opened.
findings.implication_for_boar: Do not put '1 GB' or '72%' in the maintainer package as a Google claim. Cite Unsloth as the source for the size table, and label the 72% as vendor-reported until the Google post is checked.

findings.claim: Quant sizes for Gemma 4 E2B GGUF (bartowski build, probed 2026-09-02): Q4_K_M weights 3.22 GB (default; est. 5.0 GB total at 16k ctx), Q4_K_S 3.15, IQ4_XS 3.10, Q3_K_M 3.01, Q3_K_S 2.92, IQ3_M 2.94, IQ3_XS 2.89, Q2_K 2.81, IQ2_M 2.44, Q5_K_M 3.41, Q6_K 3.63, Q8_0 4.63. Quality is shown only as tier labels: Q3 'acceptable: visible loss', Q2 'experimental: not ranked'. No perplexity or KL numbers.
findings.evidence: Fetched ModelFit E2B quant table. Sizes are measured weight files; KV totals are estimates. Page recommends Q4_K_M as default and says it never recommends 2-bit builds.
findings.implication_for_boar: Going from Q4_K_M to Q3_K_M saves only ~0.2 GB (3.22 to 3.01 GB) and Q3 has visible loss; the quant-size lever for E2B is small. Q2 saves ~0.4 GB at unranked quality. Quantization alone will not move RSS by a GB, so the quant decision is weak on memory grounds.

findings.claim: Unit check on the 3.11 GB file: the 3.22 GB Q4_K_M weight size above is decimal GB, equal to ~3.00 GiB; the 3.11 GB figure in the BOAR premise does not match any build listed by ModelFit or the Unsloth QAT table exactly. Source of the 3.11 GB file must be confirmed before using it as a baseline.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic: 3.22e9 bytes = 3.00 GiB; Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL 2.62 GB; ModelFit Q4_K_M 3.22 GB. Premise states unsloth gemma-4-E2B-it Q4_K_M at 3.11 GB.
findings.implication_for_boar: Make the memory baseline reproducible: record the exact GGUF filename, sha256 and byte size from the device, not from a table.

findings.claim: llama.cpp issue #21690 (opened 2026-04-09, closed as not planned 2026-07-26): on Gemma 4, llama-server RAM grows by several GB per generation with default checkpoints (0.7 GB to 10 GB after one generation, 18 GB after two, then OOM on a 64 GB Windows/Linux box with CUDA/Vulkan). With --ctx-checkpoints 1 and -np 1, RAM stayed near 1.5 GB. No maintainer confirmed; bug present at least since build b8660 and reported on build 8724.
findings.evidence: Fetched GitHub issue page: 'each generation is making llama-server's RAM consumption bump by several gigabytes'; table of RAM vs generations; workaround '--ctx-checkpoints 1 with -np 1' confirmed by users. Issue is on llama-server (not Android, not llama.rn), and reporter tested a 31B Heretic Q4_K_M GGUF, not E2B.
findings.implication_for_boar: Our b11010 pin is newer than the reported builds, so the bug may or may not be present; the checkpoint behaviour is a plausible contributor to 'RSS grows over a long session' on Gemma 4 and must be ruled out on the phone (set checkpoints to 1 or 0 and rerun the 73-question session, logging PSS per question).

findings.claim: Android 17 per-app memory limits: enforced first on Pixel devices running Android 17; Google expects more manufacturers to adopt them over the following year on devices from 4 GB to 16 GB+ RAM. When an app exceeds its limit the system first swaps its anonymous pages to zRAM (UI jank), then terminates the process if growth continues. Exit appears as REASON_OTHER with description 'MemoryLimiter:AnonSwap'. Google publishes no numeric thresholds per RAM tier.
findings.evidence: Fetched Android Developers Blog post by Blair Harmon: 'Per-app memory limits were introduced in Android 17, starting with Pixel devices'; 'an increasing number of manufacturers will use the Android per-app memory limits'; zRAM then termination; ApplicationExitInfo REASON_OTHER 'MemoryLimiter:AnonSwap'.
findings.implication_for_boar: A 4.5 GB PSS app on an Android 17 device could be throttled or killed without the classic LMK signature. Our 73/73 Pixel 8a run was on a pre-17 build (unverified); test the Pixel 8a on Android 17 if the OS is updated, and log ApplicationExitInfo reasons. Set an explicit PSS budget below the per-app limit the device reports via 'am memory-limiter status'.

findings.claim: Android LMK: the low memory killer daemon terminates least-essential processes under memory pressure, non-gracefully; Play vitals flags a user-perceived LMK rate above 1% of daily active users as critical. Google gives no per-process memory limit numbers on this page.
findings.evidence: Fetched Android vitals LMK page: 'The Android LMK daemon ... terminating the least essential processes'; threshold '1%'; page 'last updated 2026-10-19 UTC'.
findings.implication_for_boar: There is no published LMK threshold for an 8 GB phone; the only practical signal is our own ApplicationExitInfo logs. Use the 1% rate as a release-quality gate for the maintainer's app if it is ever shipped to Play.

findings.claim: Mapping vs locking for weights: no source found that compares mmap vs mlock for Gemma 4 on Android. Google's LiteRT card says embeddings are memory-mapped while main weights stay in memory; llama.cpp's random-access mmap handling for a large per-layer token-embedding table appears in one commit (95da4ba8) that tested a different model ('qwen4exp'), and that commit could not be opened (HTTP 429).
findings.evidence: LiteRT card quote 'LiteRT-LM framework always keeps main weights in memory, while the embedding parameters are memory mapped'. Commit page returned 429 on fetch; only a search snippet was seen for 95da4ba8.
findings.implication_for_boar: Worth a llama.cpp code read of the b11010 loader for per_layer_token_embd (is it mmapped and how are its pages counted in PSS?) before any mlock or flag change. Treat as an open engineering question, not a lever.

findings.claim: Quality at lower bits for E2B is not measured in any source found: no perplexity or KL numbers for Gemma 4 E2B at Q3_K_M, Q2_K, or IQ3 exist in the sources opened. Only qualitative tiers (Q3 visible loss, Q2 unranked). The only KL-divergence benchmark found covers the 31B model, not E2B.
findings.evidence: ModelFit E2B page gives tier labels only. A localbench substack KL study covers Gemma 4 31B GGUFs (found in search only, not opened).
findings.implication_for_boar: Any move below Q4_K_M needs our own dev-set run (2 seeds, same rubric) on the desktop before the device; the memory saving at Q3 is only ~0.2 GB, so the risk is not worth it on memory grounds alone.

open_questions: Exact memory split on the Pixel 8a for Gemma 4 E2B Q4_K_M in llama.rn b11010: how much PSS is file-backed mmap weights vs anonymous KV cache vs compute buffers vs the app's own heap. No source gives this; it needs a measured breakdown (/proc/self/smaps_rollup or dumpsys meminfo).

Does llama.cpp b11010 implement PLE caching or lazy loading of per_layer_token_embd for Gemma 4 (the Gemma 3n-style storage cache described by Google)? No source found confirms it; needs a read of the loader code.
Is the issue #21690 checkpoint RAM growth present at b11010 on Android? The issue was reported on builds 8724 and older; the phone test has to decide it.

Google's official QAT Gemma 4 E2B size and the '72%' and '~1 GB' claims: the Google Developers Blog page returned 404 and Android Authority returned 403. Need the primary Google/Hugging Face QAT model card (litert-community or google/gemma-4 QAT collection) with exact file sizes and whether a QAT GGUF exists for llama.cpp.

Google's Gemma docs page on mobile QAT (reported in search as using a wNa8o8 layout with 2-bit decoder layers for E2B/E4B) was not opened; its exact format and whether it is GGUF-compatible are unverified.

KV cache size at 4096 context for E2B: no source gives KV heads and head dim per layer for the sliding and global layers. The ~0.45 GB figure is a linear scale of ModelFit's 1.8 GB estimate at 16k, not a measurement.

Does Android 17 per-app memory limit apply to the Pixel 8a (Tensor G3) and at what limit for a 7.15 GiB visible-RAM device? Google does not publish the numbers; 'am memory-limiter status' on the phone would answer it.

Text-only GGUF: does a text-only E2B GGUF exist (vision/audio tower removed) and what size does it save? Sources found list multimodal files with mmproj; the saving from dropping the ~150M vision and ~300M audio encoders is small (~0.5 GB at F16 by parameter count, unverified) and needs a measured file.
Android-side llama.cpp commit 95da4ba8 (LLAMA_MMAP_RANDOM for a large per_layer_token_embd table) was not opened (HTTP 429); its relevance to Gemma 4 E2B on b11010 is unverified.
The 3.11 GB premise file: which exact GGUF (repo, filename, sha256) is it? None of the size tables matched it exactly.
sources_opened: https://ecorpit.com/android-app-memory-limits-oem-rollout-vitals-2026/ (opened, secondary; used only to locate the 'am memory-limiter' commands)

Failed to open (not used as evidence): https://developers.googleblog.com/en/gemma-4-quantization-aware-trained-checkpoints/ (404); https://androidauthority.com/gemma-4-qat-models-3675172/ (403); https://app.semanticdiff.com/gh/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/95da4ba86065dda8659981a508dfb52d8c3f1032 (429)

sweeps.angle: Angle 7, ecosystem and competition: Android apps shipping Gemma 4 E2B offline, poidh #31 competitors, GGUF variants and their dates/sizes, and licence terms for bundling or downloading the weights

findings.claim: Gemma 4 (including E2B) is released under Apache 2.0, replacing the earlier custom Gemma Terms of Use. Google calls it the first Gemmaverse release under an OSI-approved Apache 2.0 licence.
findings.evidence: Google Open Source Blog post dated Thursday, April 2, 2026 (URL path says 2026/03). Model lineup stated as edge models up to 31B. The unsloth and ggml-org GGUF repo pages both list license apache-2.0.
findings.implication_for_boar: Bundling the GGUF in an APK or downloading it in-app is permitted under Apache 2.0 (keep attribution/NOTICE). The licence is not a blocker for the default-model decision. Re-check the upstream model card before the public decision on 2026-10-31.

findings.claim: unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF lists Apache-2.0 and offers the Q4_K_M file at 3.11 GB, UD-Q4_K_XL at 3.18 GB, Q8_0 at 5.05 GB, Q3_K_S at 2.45 GB and UD-IQ2_M at 2.29 GB. It also ships MTP draft files (about 98 MB to 170 MB).
findings.evidence: Repo page quant table. Repo changelog: an Apr 11 re-download to pick up Google's latest chat template and llama.cpp fixes, and a Jun 9 update adding MTP support. Year is not printed on the page for the update notes.
findings.implication_for_boar: The 3.11 GB Q4_K_M we measured on the Pixel 8a is this file. The Apr 11 re-download means any GGUF older than that date may carry the older template, so the file revision must be recorded in the catalogue entry.

findings.claim: The ggml-org GGUF repo (the llama.cpp org's own conversion) offers Q4_0 at 2.84 GB, Q8_0 at 4.97 GB and BF16 at 9.31 GB, with MTP variants. It is the source Google's llama.cpp page recommends, using `llama-server -hf ggml-org/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF`.
findings.evidence: ggml-org repo page lists the quants (no Q4_K_M row). Google AI for Developers llama.cpp page recommends this repo and marks itself as deprecated, pointing to a newer site. Its last update is shown as 2026-04-16 UTC. Repo page says the conversion was automatic and its documentation is incomplete (TODOs).
findings.implication_for_boar: A Q4_0 from ggml-org (2.84 GB) is about 270 MB smaller than unsloth Q4_K_M and is the official llama.cpp-org route. Whether it is better or worse than Q4_K_M is not measured. A same-prompt A/B on device is needed before choosing one.

findings.claim: Thinking control: unsloth's model card says Transformers defaults enable_thinking=False and that thinking is triggered only by putting the <|think|> token in the system prompt. Thinking output is wrapped in <|channel>thought ... <channel|>. The card says disabled thinking does NOT leave an empty thought block on E2B and E4B (it does on other sizes).
findings.evidence: Unsloth repo model card, thinking section. Unsloth docs (zh page) say to disable thinking with --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' and to use llama-server instead of llama-cli.
findings.implication_for_boar: Our observation that llama.cpp thinks by default is not explained by this card, which describes thinking as opt-in. Likely cause: the template revision in the GGUF (see the template-defect findings). Check the actual Jinja template embedded in the exact GGUF we ship, and keep enable_thinking:false in the catalogue entry, which is consistent with the Unsloth guidance.

findings.claim: Open discussions on the official google/gemma-4-E2B-it repo report template defects: prior-turn reasoning is re-injected in multi-step tool calls, which can cause repetition loops under llama.cpp --jinja. The reporters say single-turn chat is not affected. Open PRs fix null rendering, preserve prior-turn reasoning and add validation. A patched template can be swapped into the GGUF without re-quantizing.
findings.evidence: HF discussions #36 (E2B) and #37 (E4B) describe the loop; #35 (E2B) and #36 (E4B) are the open fix PRs. A related 31B discussion (#142) reports inconsistent thought-channel opener handling. Discussion dates were not visible in the retrieved text.
findings.implication_for_boar: Our app is single-turn chat, so the loop risk is probably low, but the multi-turn LONGSESSION-style use would be exposed. Check whether the template in our shipped GGUF includes the fix, and test a 5+ turn session on the Pixel 8a before shipping Gemma as default.

findings.claim: Google's LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 page lists the E2B model at 2.58 GB and gives decode speeds of 47 tok/s (CPU) and 52 tok/s (GPU) on Samsung S26 Ultra, 25 tok/s CPU on iPhone 17 Pro, and 8 tok/s CPU on Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB. Peak CPU memory on S26 Ultra CPU is 1733 MB. There is no Pixel or Tensor G3 row.
findings.evidence: developers.google.com/edge/litert-lm/models/gemma-4 table (prefill, decode, TTFT, peak CPU mem). Benchmark methodology is not described on the page beyond device and backend. Page last updated 2026-09-04 UTC. Thinking mode is not mentioned.
findings.implication_for_boar: Google's own published speed is for LiteRT-LM, a different runtime from our llama.cpp GGUF path, so it is not a direct comparison with our Pixel 8a numbers (10.5 tok/s short run, 7.0 tok/s sustained). It sets a plausible ceiling, not a target. No Tensor G3 number exists in what we found.

findings.claim: Google AI Edge Gallery is an official Google app that downloads and runs Gemma 4 E2B on-device offline. It has a built-in benchmark that runs a fixed prompt and reports prefill tok/s, decode tok/s and peak RSS, reached from the Models Management screen. It uses LiteRT-LM, not GGUF.
findings.evidence: Secondary coverage only (pasqualepillitteri.it, decrypt.co, codersera). Coverage says the model downloads separately after install, and one blog puts it at about 1.3 GB and another at about 2.58 GB for E2B.
findings.implication_for_boar: Use the Gallery app's built-in benchmark on the Pixel 8a as an independent reference: it gives a same-phone, same-model-family number from Google's own stack, which is a cheap sanity check on our 7 tok/s sustained figure. Verify the app's date and version before quoting it.

findings.claim: OfflineLLM (github.com/jegly/OfflineLLM) is an open-source Android app that runs any GGUF through llama.cpp, lists gemma-4-E2B-it at about 1.3 GB for Q4_K_M, and recommends it for 6-8 GB RAM devices. It is Apache-2.0 and its llama.cpp submodule is pinned at commit 60eeeb6. No speed or memory benchmarks are given, and no release date is visible.
findings.evidence: GitHub README. The 1.3 GB figure conflicts with unsloth's Q4_K_M of 3.11 GB for the same model family, so one of the two is likely a different quant or a README error.
findings.implication_for_boar: This is the nearest existing shipping analogue (Gemma 4 E2B, GGUF, llama.cpp, Android, offline). Its 1.3 GB claim should not be quoted until we check the actual file. Its thinking handling is undocumented in the README, which is a gap to check directly if we want a comparison.

findings.claim: Other Android offline-LLM apps named in a third-party comparison: PocketPal AI (open source, llama.cpp-based, can search Hugging Face in-app) and Off Grid (offline-first, llama.cpp-based). Neither was checked for Gemma 4 E2B support.
findings.evidence: Single third-party blog summary (aitoolranked.com comparison). No primary source opened.
findings.implication_for_boar: Candidates for a competitor/adoption check. Do not treat as confirmed Gemma 4 shippers until their repos or release notes are read.

findings.claim: The poidh bounty #31 page asks for an Android offline research assistant that reaches at least half the quality of internet search plus frontier AI, on hardware with at most 12 GB RAM. Submissions must be a public demo plus a repo whose working version exists at claim time.
findings.evidence: Search result snippet from poidh.xyz bounty page (not opened in full). Several public repos appear for the bounty: a competitor team's repo (BOAR), UPSTREAM_REPO/boar-app, a competitor team/commonplace (Wikipedia-only retrieval, no INTERNET permission), a competitor team's repo (cites each number to a passage), a competitor team's repo (no language model), a competitor team's repo competitor team (Android-first, llama.cpp-based). None of their READMEs were opened for model choice.
findings.implication_for_boar: Competitors are not shown to use Gemma 4 E2B yet. Open their READMEs and release notes to check the model they ship. a competitor team's no-network design means its ceiling is retrieval quality, not model choice, so it is less of a model benchmark than the others.

findings.claim: Google's own Gemma 4 llama.cpp docs and the unsloth docs both recommend llama-server with the chat template flags for thinking control, and Google's page says it has been superseded.
findings.evidence: ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/integrations/llamacpp: llama-cli -hf and llama-server -hf commands; no enable_thinking or reasoning flag mentioned; last updated 2026-04-16 UTC; marked deprecated.
findings.implication_for_boar: Do not rely on Google's llama.cpp page for the thinking flag; the authoritative flag is the unsloth/template evidence above. Confirm the flag by running the pinned b11010 binary with the shipped GGUF.

findings.claim: vLLM issue #39130 reports that combining the gemma4 reasoning parser with enable_thinking:false silently disables xgrammar structured-output enforcement (reported on E4B, said to apply to other Gemma 4 variants).
findings.evidence: GitHub vLLM issue 39130 as listed in search results; text read via search excerpt only.
findings.implication_for_boar: Only relevant if the app enforces JSON or grammar output. The llama.cpp path is different and not verified. Test grammar/JSON output with enable_thinking:false on the pinned build before relying on it.

findings.claim: No Pixel 8 or Tensor G3 benchmark for Gemma 4 E2B was found in any source. A community M2 Pro Mac result (runtime not stated) reports about 66 tok/s at 1k context, falling to about 46 at 32k.
findings.evidence: omlx.ai community benchmark listing; search excerpt. Pixel 8 absent from Google, Hugging Face mirror and community tables.
findings.implication_for_boar: Our Pixel 8a measurements are the only Tensor G3 data point for this model. Publishing them as a public reference (with the caveat that the runtime is llama.cpp and the thermal status was 1 mid-run) would fill a real gap in the ecosystem.

Which GGUF revision (unsloth Q4_K_M, or ggml-org Q4_0) is the one the maintainer's catalogue will point to, and is its embedded Jinja template the fixed one? Needs a direct read of the GGUF metadata or the file's tokenizer.chat_template, not done here.
